A1.justification: Both PDFs describe IC-Custom and share identifiable methods, datasets and experiments. All pages were inspected, including v2's supplementary figures and v3's Appendices A–L. Text extraction and visual inspection support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original ProductBench and DreamBench evaluations, a 20-participant human study, ablations and multi-reference voting results.

after.justification: v3 retains original benchmark and human-study results and reports additional ICMA ablations, ACE++ comparisons and qualitative analyses.

M1.justification: The framework, task registers, Redux branch and multi-reference index embeddings are retained; CE/TE become RE/FE, and the multi-reference extension moves to Appendix H. However, v3 revises text-query/key rotary terms in Eq. 6 and explicitly specifies logit-normal timestep weighting. The PDFs do not resolve whether these reflect procedural changes or corrections and disclosures of the existing implementation.

E1.justification: Training coverage remains 12K real/synthetic diptychs plus 4K multi-reference polyptychs, with the latter retained in Appendix H. ProductBench, DreamBench and the position-aware, position-free and multi-reference tasks remain represented. The added comparisons and examples do not establish a distinct new dataset, domain or task.

E2.justification: ACE++, previously discussed without evaluated results, is newly compared against IC-Custom on ProductBench using its released subject LoRA adapters (Appendix E, Table 4 and Figure 10). The external comparator membership in the main benchmark and human-study tables is retained.

E3.justification: v2's DreamBench protocol comparing diptych and polyptych models with 1–3 references using GPT-4o votes is removed; v3 provides a qualitative comparison in Appendix H. New experiments disable task registers or positional embeddings and evaluate ACE++ subject LoRA adapters. The retained single-reference benchmarks and 20-participant, 50-sample human study keep their stated settings.

E4.justification: v3 directly ablates both central ICMA innovations through w/o TR and w/o PE controls (Table 3(b)), extends the ablation visualization and adds boundary-artifact cases (Appendix B, Figure 7). Conversely, v2's quantitative reference-count analysis disappears, replaced by a sunglasses case study. This substantially revises the evidence testing the proposed components and multi-reference behavior.

E5.justification: The new application screenshots disclose fixed example seeds and a '-1 for random' option (Figures 14–15), information absent from v2. This is limited seed disclosure: neither version reports repeated-run counts or benchmark uncertainty estimates, and the screenshots do not establish multi-seed evaluation.

E6.justification: Main benchmark scores, human preferences and retained ablation scores are unchanged. v3 adds ACE++ results, including precise/user-drawn DINO-I scores of 60.68/61.26 versus IC-Custom's 63.14/63.28, and adds w/o TR and w/o PE results. It removes v2 Figure 7's voting results and adds or revises qualitative outputs, changing supporting evidence while retaining headline rankings.

T1.justification: v3 expresses the loss with explicit logit-normal timestep weighting, whereas v2 displays an unweighted time integral. It also introduces conditional-distribution definitions for task unification and revises ICMA's text-token rotary terms. These are limited formal additions and revisions; no theorem, proof or theoretical guarantee is added.

C1.justification: The central unification, real-data, efficiency and performance claims remain. However, v3 reframes multi-reference customization from comprehensive support within the main contribution to a preliminary extension in the conclusion and Appendix H. Its abstract emphasizes the 12K diptych dataset instead of the combined 16K training collection.

C2.justification: v3 connects boundary confusion more explicitly to jointly modeling reference and output images and explains multi-view benefits through missing sunglasses-temple details. Limitations expand from viewpoint and lighting to geometry and other 3D properties. The earlier interpretation of degradation with increasing reference count is removed, while multi-reference applicability is qualified as preliminary.

D1.justification: v3 adds exact captioning prompts, mask-sampling probabilities, morphological augmentation operations, the GPT-4o version date and a Gradio inference workflow. It also promises code, model and application releases. Conversely, v2's four-token register size and 10K multi-reference training budget are no longer specified. These substantially change reproducibility documentation without establishing that existing experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: ACE++ receives a focused comparison concerning its task-specific LoRAs, Long-context Condition Unit and absence of ICMA. v3 adds flow-matching, rectified-flow, T5 and Gemini references and removes In-context LoRA and OminiControl2 references. Most previous related-work content is retained in Appendix A.

P1.justification: The introduction, method and experimental discussion are extensively rewritten. Preliminaries becomes a standalone section, related work moves to Appendix A, and additional appendix sections organize technical and application documentation. Terminology changes include ProductData to CustomData, target image to fill-in image and CE/TE to RE/FE, accompanying substantial narrative restructuring.

P2.justification: The paper switches from two-column to single-column layout and redraws the architecture and ICMA diagrams. Human-study columns move from v2 Table 2 into v3 Table 3(a), beside expanded ablations. Captioning, boundary-analysis, ACE++, multi-reference and application visuals are added; existing galleries are rearranged and expanded, while the voting chart is removed.

improvement.justification: Direct ICMA ablations, the ACE++ comparison and newly supplied mask/captioning details improve support and reproducibility for the core contribution. These gains are limited by the loss of quantitative multi-reference validation and some training details. The new ethics statement also contradicts the retained 20-participant study. Overall, the core work is better documented and empirically supported, with a modest net improvement.
